findings.obs_text: In Act 17:2, Act 17:17, Act 18:4, Act 18:19 and Act 19:8 the verb of reasoning (G1256) is qualified by time, frequency and place: on three Sabbaths, every day, every Sabbath, for three months, and there in Ephesus. The qualifiers tell when and how often Paul reasoned, not how.
In 1Cor 13:11 the verb reasoned (G3049) is qualified by a comparison, like a child (G3516), the same qualifier set on spoke and thought before it; the adjective returns as the childish ways given up.

In Jam 3:17 the subgroup's word is itself a qualifier: open to reason (G2138, an adjective) is one of a series of qualities said of the wisdom from above, with pure, peaceable, gentle, full of mercy, impartial and sincere, ordered by first and then.
In Act 28:18 a negator reaches the subgroup's word itself: no (G3367) qualifies the cause (G0156), so the verse denies that any ground for the death penalty was found.
findings.grounds: no reason for the death penalty

findings.obs_text: In Pro 3:30 the subgroup's word works as a qualifier of the verb: for no reason (H2600, an adverb, without cause) qualifies contend; the negator not (H0408) reaches contend and no (H3808) reaches harm, not the reason.

Where the subgroup's word is a phrase of cause, the negators of the verse reach other words, not the cause: unknown in Gen 41:31 (the plenty), bear, profane and die in Num 18:32, has not come in 1Sa 20:29, the question and know in Mar 12:24, no longer bear in 1Th 3:5.
findings.grounds: neither the Scriptures nor the power of God

findings.obs_text: In Gen 41:31, Gen 47:13 and Eze 19:10 the phrase by reason of governs a noun of cause, and the qualifiers reach that noun: the famine that will follow and is very severe, the abundant water.

In the other verses the qualifiers stand in the clause around the subgroup's word and reach other words: males in Jos 5:4, now in 1Sa 20:29, branches in Eze 19:10, Most High, lives, forever and everlasting of God in Dan 4:34, more greatness in Dan 4:36, vicious crime in Act 18:14, alarmed Felix and the present in Act 24:25, often in Rom 15:22, vain labor in 1Th 3:5, all distress in 1Th 3:7, foremost, perfect and eternal in 1Ti 1:16, always, prepared and anyone in 1Pe 3:15. The devil in 1Jo 3:8 is marked an adjective in the data but stands as a noun.

older.finding: fear at an act of power that leads people to ask Jesus to go (Mark 5:15, Luke 8:35 and 8:37), and Felix alarmed at Paul's reasoning (Acts 24:25): a working of fear, for the fear collection
older.reason: it states how fear works; its nodes are words of the fear collection

older.finding: a face of the fear words: fear felt before God's presence, act or word, or a messenger
older.reason: it states which faces the fear surfaces show in their verses; its nodes are words of the fear and wise collections

it states what the qualifier above gives by the grammar to what it is joined to (priority, superiority or origin), as in the wisdom from above of Jas 3:17; a statement of the structure, not of the inner being
